measures.what_it_does: Lets the hospital district that runs Three Rivers Hospital in Brewster issue up to $48 million in bonds over as long as 30 years to remodel, renovate and re-equip the hospital. The district reaches from Okanogan County into northern Douglas County; supporters say it serves communities from Mansfield to Mazama. A $45 million version got 52.3% in November 2025 and failed. Needs 60% to pass.
measures.cost_line: About $0.73 per $1,000 of assessed value, roughly $219 a year ($18 a month) on a $300,000 home, for up to 30 years.
measures.pro_summary: The statement in favor (Michael Pruett, the hospital board's chair) says the bond keeps quality care close to home at a community-owned hospital. It calls the project a practical upgrade of patient spaces, technology and infrastructure, and links local care to wildfire and emergency resilience.
measures.con_summary: The statement against (Melvin Sorensen) says voters should first get county-wide information on how best to meet Okanogan County's medical needs, and that $48 million and 30 years of taxes would lock in the current system; a county-wide study might favor a central facility with outlying urgent care centers. His rebuttal adds that the county's three small hospitals compete with each other, that Three Rivers is fragile, and that if it failed residents would pay for decades with no hospital.

taxes.basis: A yes vote adds a new excess property tax of about $0.73 per $1,000 for up to 30 years to repay up to $48 million in bonds. The hospital's hope of later ending its ER operating levy is not part of the measure.

measures.sources_note: Sources: VoteWA voters' guide record 7283 (S1); the official sample ballot (S2); the hospital's proposal, cost and FAQ pages (S3-S5); VoteWA record 6866 and Secretary of State results for the November 2025 bond (S6, S7); RCW 84.52.056 (S8).

measures.what_it_does: Renews the Waterville-area hospital district's one-year operating levy, which pays for its ambulance service and a clinic contracted with Wenatchee Valley Medical Center. The district asks for the same levy every year; voters approved it in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025. Needs 60% to pass.
measures.cost_line: $80,000 in 2027, about $0.36 per $1,000 of assessed value (about $108 on a $300,000 property). The 2025 and 2026 levies were the same amount and rate.
measures.pro_summary: No statement in favor was filed. The district says the levy provides sufficient funds for its clinic and ambulance services.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed, and no opposing committee is listed.

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews the district's recurring one-year levy at the same $80,000 and $0.36 per $1,000 as the last two years. It is a renewal, not a new tax.

measures.sources_note: Sources: VoteWA voters' guide record 7320 (S1); the official sample ballot (S2); district Resolution #91 (S3); VoteWA records for the 2025 and 2026 levies (S4, S5); Secretary of State results for 2020-2025 (S6-S9); RCW 84.52.052 (S10). No news coverage was found.

measures.what_it_does: Lets Eastmont School District borrow $125 million in bonds, repaid by property taxes over up to 20 years. The money rebuilds the oldest parts of Kenroy, Lee and Cascade elementary schools, built 1957-1967, replacing 15 portables, and pays for security entrances, roofs, HVAC, parking and athletic upgrades at other schools. The district expects about $25 million in state aid. Bonds failed in 2022 and twice in 2024, the 2024 tries just under 60%. Needs 60% to pass.
measures.cost_line: The district estimates $0.79 per $1,000 of assessed value for 20 years, about $395 a year ($32.92 a month) on a $500,000 home. It does not say whether that is on top of the current school rate.
measures.pro_summary: The statement in favor (Alejandro C. Cruz, Dr. Gene Sharratt and Dr. Sue Kane) says the three elementaries are aging, overcrowded and costly to maintain. It says the bond replaces 15 portables, eliminates 162 exterior classroom doors with secure entrances and interior halls, moves pickup away from busy streets, and qualifies Eastmont for about $25 million in state funds.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed; the county says no one came forward to serve on an opposing committee.

taxes.basis: A yes vote authorizes $125 million in new bonds repaid by an excess property tax the district estimates at $0.79 per $1,000 for 20 years.

measures.sources_note: Sources: VoteWA voters' guide record 7321 (S1); the official sample ballot (S2); the district's 2026, 2024 and 2022 bond pages (S3-S5); NCWLIFE on the board's vote and the facilities committee (S6, S7); Secretary of State results for 2022 and both 2024 elections (S8-S10); RCW 84.52.056 (S11).

measures.what_it_does: Forms a new fire protection district for the Rimrock Meadows area of Douglas County (about 29 square miles; Ephrata mailing addresses), which is in no fire district today, run by three elected commissioners and paid for by property taxes. Only voters inside the proposed boundary vote. The three commissioner races on the same ballot fill its first board if it forms. The ballot statement says a majority forms it; state law (RCW 52.02.110) says three-fifths.
measures.cost_line: No levy is set by this vote. Once formed, the board may levy up to $0.50 per $1,000 (RCW 52.16.130), plus up to $0.50 each under RCW 52.16.140 and 52.16.160, within state limits.
measures.pro_summary: The statement in favor (committee: Gerald Dotson, Christine Crisler and Truman Crisler) is a resident's account of three wildfire evacuation notices since 2017, including a three-day evacuation in 2020, and says this part of the county has been overlooked for a fire district.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed; the county says no one came forward to serve on an opposing committee.

taxes.basis: A yes vote creates a new property-taxing district where none exists. No rate is set by this vote, though state law lets the board levy up to $0.50 per $1,000 and more, so the lean is weaker.

measures.sources_note: Sources: VoteWA voters' guide record 7425 (S1); the official sample ballot (S2); county Resolutions CE 26-19B and CE 26-25 (S3); the Wenatchee World on the Auditor's announcement (S4); the county's fire district and address GIS records (S5, S6); RCW 52.02.080, 52.02.110, 52.16.130, 52.16.140 and 52.16.160 (S7-S11).

measures.what_it_does: Renews the yearly maintenance levy for the cemetery district that runs seven cemeteries and a mausoleum in the Waterville area, paying for upkeep and irrigation. The levy for 2025 fell short of 60% and the district cut irrigation; the 2026 levy passed. Needs 60% to pass.
measures.cost_line: $50,000 in 2027, about $0.22 per $1,000 of assessed value (about $66 on a $300,000 property). The 2026 levy was $60,000 at about $0.25.
measures.pro_summary: The statement in favor (Jenna Dixon, Sandra Stoddard and Terri Thomsen) says the levy keeps cemetery services affordable, keeps up the rural cemeteries and restores normal irrigation with upgraded systems.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed; the county says no one came forward to serve on an opposing committee.

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews the district's recurring one-year maintenance levy, $10,000 smaller than 2026's at a lower estimated rate. It is a renewal, not a new tax.

measures.sources_note: Sources: VoteWA voters' guide record 7322 (S1); the official sample ballot (S2); district Resolution #2026/001 (S3); VoteWA records for the 2025 and 2026 levies (S4, S5); Secretary of State results for 2020-2025 (S6-S9); RCW 84.52.052 (S10). No news coverage was found.
